messages:
Nadia: follow-up from the auth design sync: we need to settle env scoping for API keys (dev/stage/prod) and how service principals cross project boundaries.
Eli: proposal: keys are (project, env) scoped by default. cross-project calls require either an explicit service-binding or a short-lived delegated token. this prevents accidental prod access from dev.
Ravi: +1. practically, a lot of infra scripts run across projects. we should support service-bindings for infra-only principals with tight RBAC and an allowlist.
Josef: for service-bindings, do we mint JWTs with claims: {sub, proj, env, svc_binding_id, iat, exp}? that gives traceability and lets downstream enforce env.
Claire: thoughts on naming claims: use "proj" and "env" vs full resource arn? shorter claims are nicer for logs. but include resource-version for long-lived bindings.
Nadia: also want to avoid adding too many in-path calls. broker option: 1) in-path mint (sync) 2) async mint + short-lived cache 3) pre-warm on deployment. tradeoffs: sync adds latency, async needs recheck on miss.
Eli: measurement: sync mint ~10ms median, worst-case 35ms. acceptable for most service calls, but for high-qps model inference we need pre-warm + cache.
Ravi: two additional constraints: 1) fail-open vs fail-closed when broker unavailable. for cross-project delegations we should fail-closed; for same-project reads we can allow cached tokens. document modes per route.
Josef: RBAC model: keep roles for humans (admin, dev, viewer) and move service permissions to capability-sets (e.g., embed:read, model:invoke:low-prio). service bindings reference capability IDs. capability IDs are namespaced by org.
Claire: auditing: we must record both the original service principal and the minted actor in logs. suggest fields: caller_principal, actor_jti, binding_id, effective_capabilities. also support sampling of full request payloads for sec incidents.
Nadia: migration plan for keys that are currently global: detect keys used from multiple envs -> create migration ticket + suggest split keys. offer an automated split wizard that rewrites deploy configs with new keys.
Eli: compatibility TTL: mark old global keys as "legacy" and enforce rotation in 60 days unless owner opts out with justification, logged auditable.
Ravi: emergency breakglass: we need a revoke-by-cookie mechanism for operator keys used during incidents. propose a one-time-signed breakglass token stored in vault that sets a live override for 15 minutes and is fully audited.
Josef: header surface: keep Authorization: Bearer <token>. add optional header X-Delegated-By for debug, but primary propagation should be via JWT claims (deleg field). proxies may drop custom headers.
Claire: Console features: per-key timeline (envs used, last seen IP, routes accessed), an "associated bindings" view that shows which projects and services depend on a key. exportable CSV.
Nadia: next steps: create a short follow-up RFC covering: env scoping defaults, service-binding model, JWT claim schema, broker fail modes, migration TTLs, and breakglass design.
Eli: I'll draft the broker fail-mode matrix + perf notes. Ravi can draft capability naming and binding API. Josef, can you draft the JWT claim schema and audit fields?
Josef: yes. will include sample JWTs and a small test plan that asserts env denial for cross-env tokens.
Nadia: tagging @security-bot to create tasks. will review drafts in 4 days.
security-bot: created tasks SEC-7991 (Draft env-scoping RFC) assigned to Nadia, SEC-7992 (Broker fail-mode & perf) assigned to Eli, SEC-7993 (Capability model + bindings) assigned to Ravi, SEC-7994 (JWT schema + audit) assigned to Josef. due in 4 days. :calendar:
